create_maglev.ponder.traction_substation: New Age generators feed a traction substation through electrical connectors and copper wire.
Bogey pickups draw from nearby substations within the configured supply radius: 64 blocks by default.
A redstone signal opens the breaker and isolates supply; stored energy remains in the substation.
A comparator reads stored charge. Engineer's Goggles show charge, breaker state, and output.
Each substation has a rated output per tick. Add substations for heavy or many trains; weak supply lowers acceleration and top speed instead of stopping the train.
create_maglev.ponder.maglev.text_1: Maglev bogeys run only on the dedicated Maglev Guideway, not ordinary Create track.
create_maglev.ponder.maglev.text_2: Levitation and propulsion are separate: magnetic lift raises the carriage, while a linear motor along the guideway drives it forward.
create_maglev.ponder.maglev.text_3: With traction power available, the whole carriage rises 0.25 blocks above the guideway.
create_maglev.ponder.maglev.text_4: When power is lost, the train brakes and the carriage settles back onto the guideway.
create_maglev.ponder.electric_bullet_bog: Electric bogeys run on ordinary Create track when their pickups receive substation power.
Bullet bogeys reach their higher speed only on Reinforced Standard Track.
Curve speed depends on radius: a gentle, wide curve permits faster travel than a tight bend.
Every wheeled tier can use reinforced track, but only bullet bogeys gain speed from it.
Learn how substations supply electric and maglev trains.
